resources.string: This application was created to demonstrate the methods of detecting VPN and Proxy according to the officially approved methodology. The tool is designed to show that to hide the fact of circumvention, a comprehensive approach is required, bypassing a set of independent checks.
Server-side analysis. Comparison of IP with reputation databases.
Comparison of IPv4 and IPv6 geolocations to detect bypass traffic.
Querying the Android billing API for TRANSPORT_VPN and VpnTransportInfo.
Detecting proxy settings based on System.getProperty system properties.
Search for installed known VPN/Proxy clients and bypass tools.
Checking for the NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_VPN flag in active network connections.
Search for virtual tunneling adapters (tun, tap, wg, ppp).
Analysis of frame size (MTU) for traces of VPN header encapsulation.
Checking standard ports (Socks5/HTTP) opened by client proxies.
Checking if fake local IP addresses are returned to domains (Fake-IP tunneling).
Comparison of ping to national (RU) and European (EU) nodes.
The method determines the IP region on the server side (GeoIP).
Use residential proxies or configure split routing (Split Tunneling) to Russian IP addresses.
Circumvention is reliably hidden at the GeoIP level.
Could not retrieve server response with GeoIP.
The system directly reports an active VPN tunnel.
Use Proxy mode (bypassing VpnService) or VPN clients with root access (e.g. iptables) for transparent redirection without system flags.
Detection of system proxy usage based on System.getProperty system properties.
Disable system proxy settings in Android network settings for traffic to go directly.
Indirect evidence. This flag is present in physical network connections and missing when VPN is active.
Use socket-level bypasses that do not register VPN in the system.
Indirect evidence. Presence of virtual interfaces (tun/tap/wg) may indicate a tunnel.
Do not create a tun interface in client settings (use raw socks/http proxy), or rename the interface using root access.
Indirect check of virtual tunnel adapters.
Direct evidence. Popular installed VPN clients detected.
Use custom builds/forks of clients or hide apps using Magisk modules / App Hider.
Check for popular installed VPN clients.
Indirect evidence. Lowered MTU is typical for tunneled traffic due to header encapsulation.
Adjust the MTU of the virtual interface to standard values (1420-1500) in advanced VPN client settings.
Analysis of frame size (MTU) for indirect traces of VPN encapsulation.
Indirect evidence. Open ports can indicate a local Proxy/Xray/Socks5 server is running.
Change the default incoming port (1080, 10808) to random dynamic ports (e.g. 49211) in the client configuration.
Analysis of open local ports typical for proxy clients.
Indirect evidence. The VPN core (e.g. Xray/sing-box) spoofs IPs to intercept traffic.
Disable Fake-IP function in DNS settings (switch to Real-IP, redir-host or remote DNS).
Checking for fake internal IP addresses mapping to popular servers (Fake-IP tunneling).
Analysis of RTT to control landmarks.
Too low ping (<= 2ms) is impossible in real networks and indicates TCP intercept by a local proxy.
Exclude verification hosts from TUN/Proxy intercept (use direct routing).
Abnormally high latency to local (RU) node compared to foreign (EU) node indicates VPN usage.
Disconnect VPN or add local hosts (ya.ru) to exclusions.
Comparing ping (TCP RTT) for national and foreign nodes.
LEAK! IPv4 is encrypted (%1$s), but IPv6 goes directly (%2$s, Country: %3$s)
CLEAN (IPv6: %1$s, but country not defined - leak unlikely)
CLEAN (IPv6 connection did not return address)
CLEAN (IPv6 is not supported or blocked by tunnel)
Determining real IPv6 address leak. Common VPN vulnerability where IPv6 traffic goes around the tunnel.
Analysis of real IPv6 address leak via unprotected routes.
Disable IPv6 in your mobile network settings or router settings. Some VPN clients also allow forced blocking of non-tunneled IPv6 traffic.
Methodology of detecting signs of bypass tools usage on client devices. Recognized text in Markdown format.
Please select your preferred app language and target GeoIP region to start. The target region is the country you expect to be geolocated in when no VPN is active.
Country code must be exactly 2 letters (e.g. US)
